data.long_meaning: Trilochan is a Sanskrit word that means 'three-eyed God'. It is a name for Lord Shiva, who is believed to have three eyes. The name Trilochan carries the meaning “Three-eyed God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Trilochan usually hope their child will grow to embody three-eyed god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: According to Puranic scriptures, Trilochan was a revered sage and the chief preceptor of the celestial students or Devagitas. The term 'Trilochan' refers to the three eyes of the sage. He is considered to be a manifestation of Lord Shiva.

Another reference to Trilochan is found in the epic Mahabharata. He is mentioned as a sage who performed severe penance to please Lord Shiva. Trilochan is also known for his role in the battle of Kurukshetra, where he advised Yudhishthira, the eldest Pandava brother, on various matters.
